notes: §1985:XI.4.1.3 SR1: 'A MERGE statement may appear anywhere in the Procedure Division except in the declaratives portion.' SortBinder.ScreenDeclarativePlacement refuses a MERGE (COBOL2700) when EnclosingContext.InDeclarative holds, which BinderContext.Enclosing answers from DeclarativeAtCursor and, since kb/Work PB5275, from ProcedureTableBuilder.InDebuggingSection, so a debugging section (in the declaratives, §1985:XV.3.2.3 SR1) is covered; GateSortMergeProcedures applies the 2023 MERGE-in-procedure ban only at 2023. Probes at --std 85 (classes b, c, e): refused a MERGE in a USE FOR DEBUGGING section under WITH DEBUGGING MODE, and one nested two IFs deep in the second paragraph of an ALL PROCEDURES debugging section followed by a USE AFTER ERROR section; without DEBUGGING MODE the debugging section is a comment (§1985:XV) and the program runs DONE; a MERGE in a main-line paragraph PERFORMed from a declarative compiles and runs (the rule is lexical; COBOL2375 is the separate declarative-reference warning); a MERGE in another MERGE's output procedure compiles at 85 and prints AAAA BBBB CCCC DONE, refused COBOL1572 at --std 2023; sequential USING/GIVING files merge in key order. The 85 message cites §2023:14.9.24.3 SR1 rather than the 1985 rule. The witness, a MERGE in a USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR section, is refused COBOL2700. next.reason: 1985: "may appear anywhere in the Procedure Division except in the declaratives portion"; 2023: "except in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement, or in an output procedure of another MERGE statement". 2023 keeps the declaratives ban but adds bans: exception-checking PERFORM, another MERGE's output procedure, and file SORT input/output procedures. The 1985 rule states only declaratives.
